prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Dallas after a truck accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — before I give specific firm names, a quick question: do you want a local Dallas boutique (often more personalized, local trial experience) or a large regional/national firm (more resources to investigate big trucking companies)? Also, how severe were the injuries (minor, serious, catastrophic/fatal)? That helps me tailor recommendations.

Until you answer, here’s practical, immediate guidance plus what to ask any firm you call (so you can start contacting firms right away).

What to look for in a truck-accident lawyer
- Trucking-specific experience: cases against commercial carriers, experience with FMCSA rules, black box/ELD data, and hiring expert accident reconstructionists.  
- Trial experience and verdicts: many insurers won’t settle big cases unless the firm can credibly try the case.  
- Resources: ability to hire investigators, medical experts, economists, and to pursue claims against multiple defendants (driver, motor carrier, maintenance shops, manufacturers).  
- Good reputation: board certifications (Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Personal Injury Trial Law), AV or peer-review ratings, and client reviews.  
- Fee structure: contingency fee (no upfront attorney fee, lawyer paid only if you recover). Make sure you understand expenses and how they’re handled.

Types of firms to call
- Local Dallas trial firms that handle commercial vehicle cases (good local knowledge and court relationships).  
- Large Texas firms (Houston/Dallas/Austin) known for high-value personal injury and trucking cases (more investigative resources).  
- National plaintiff firms with Dallas presence (big advertising but large resources for trucking litigation).

Sample questions to ask when you call
1. Do you handle truck (commercial vehicle) accident cases? How many per year?  
2. Have you tried truck-accident cases to a jury in Dallas County (or Texas) recently? What were the outcomes?  
3. Do you have experience with FMCSA/ELD/black-box evidence and hiring accident reconstructionists?  
4. Who will be my main point of contact — lead attorney or a team?  
5. What is your fee structure and how are case expenses handled?  
6. Will you file suit right away if needed? What’s the typical timeline?  
7. Do you take cases on contingency only, and are there any case types you won’t accept?  
8. Can you provide references or client reviews for similar cases?

What to have ready for your first call/consultation
- Date/time/location of crash, photos, police report number (if you have it)  
- Names/insurance of other parties, truck company name, DOT/US DOT number (if available)  
- Medical records or summary of injuries / treating doctors  
- Wage information (if missed work)  
- Any video (dashcam, traffic cams, surveillance) or witness contact info

Immediate steps (do now)
- Seek/continue medical care and keep records.  
- Preserve evidence (photos, videos, damaged property).  
- Do not give a recorded statement to the trucking company’s insurer without speaking to a lawyer.  
- Contact 3–5 firms and compare: responsiveness, experience, and who will handle the case.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a curated list of Dallas-area firms that commonly handle truck accidents (I’ll need to know whether you prefer local boutiques or larger firms, and I’ll include why to call each and what to expect).  
- Draft a short script you can use on calls.

Which would you prefer?
